column2: One should worship the Vardhani, Vighnaraja, the teacher and the Self. Then, smeared with all herbs, fumigated, with flowers and durva,
having invited that sacred thread and placed it within the joined hands: "Om, to fill all gaps of rite and for the rite,
I invite you, origin, bringer of the fulfillment of your wish; grant its accomplishment to the worshipper, lord of the conscious and unconscious.
In every way, always, Shambhu, homage to you; be gracious to me. You are invited, lord of gods, with the Goddess, with the lords of the hosts,
with the lords of mantras and the guardians of the world with attendants. I invite you; in the morning the sacred thread,
and I shall observe the vow, supreme lord, at your command." Having thus invited the god, made nectar-like by exhalation,
having uttered the root-mantra ending with Shiva, one should offer it to Shiva. Having done repetition, praise and the measure, one should ask Shambhu's forgiveness.
Having offered, one should give a third part of the porridge to Shiva's fire; to the directional deities, lords of the directions, the hosts of elements and mothers,
to the Rudras, field-guardians and others, "Homage, svaha — this is the offering"; with elephants of the quarters and others in the east and others, to the field and to Agni an offering.
Having rinsed, one should perform the oblation that fills gaps in rite; having made the full oblation and the utterance-oblation one should enclose the fire.
Then "Om, to Agni, svaha; to Soma, svaha; Om, to Agni and Soma, svaha; to Agni Svishtakrit" likewise.
Having given the fourfold oblation, one should make the yoking: the god worshipped in the fire-pit, Shiva worshipped in the mandala,
then by rule one should join them in the form of joining of channels; having placed in a bamboo vessel the missile and then the heart,
having placed on them the sacred threads one should consecrate with digits or with Brahma and root-mantras, the six limbs, or join the heart, dharma and missile.
Having made them with threads and wrapped, having worshipped with things arising from the limbs, humbled with devotion one should offer them to the lord of the world for protection.
Having worshipped with flowers, incense and the rest, having given in the book of doctrine, having gone to the teacher's feet one should devotedly give the sacred thread.
Having gone out and rinsed outside, in three circles of cow-dung, one should worship in order the five cow-products, porridge and tooth-stick.
Having rinsed, bound to the mantra, having kept a musical vigil, the seeker of enjoyment should sleep on a bed of darbha, inwardly remembering the Lord.
In just this manner the seeker of liberation too should lie, only on a bed of ash, fasting and composed.
Having uttered the mantra ending with Shiva, the sacred thread should be given to him. In the protectors of all causes, having uttered Shiva, of good vows,
having uttered the root ending in dissolution, one should give the Gangavataraka. The thread for seekers of liberation is declared by the Self-knowledge Shivas;
for seekers of enjoyment it is indicated in order by the Shiva-principle beings. One should utter their mantra ending in svaha or in namah.

Om Ham, to the lord of the Self-principle, Shiva, svaha. Om Ham, to the lord of the knowledge-principle, Shiva, svaha. Om Haum, to the lord of the Shiva-principle, Shiva, svaha. Om Haum, to the lord of all principles, Shiva, svaha. Having bowed to the Gangavataraka, with joined hands one should pray: "You are the refuge of all beings, you stand in the moving and unmoving;
by moving within beings you, supreme lord, are the seer. By action, mind and speech, I have no other refuge than you.
What I have done without mantra, without rite, without materials, without repetition, oblation and worship, daily for you,
and what is undone or without proper speech, fill that, great Lord. You, supreme lord, are the best-purified, the sin-destroying purifier;
by you all the world, moving and unmoving, is purified. Whatever vow has been broken by me, god, through defect of procedure,
let all that become one, strung on the thread of your command." Having offered the repetition to the god and made a hymn with devotion,
having bowed, the man should take up the vow told by the teacher: four months, three months, three days or one day.
Having bowed and asked forgiveness of the Lord, the vower, going to the pit, thus the four sacred threads even on Shiva in the fire,
having placed and worshipped with flowers, incense, rice and the rest, one should offer the inner offering and the sacred thread to the Rudras and others.
Having entered within and praised Shiva, with bowing one should ask forgiveness. Having made the expiatory oblation and offered the pudding,
slowly giving the full oblation, one should dismiss Shiva from the fire. Having made the oblation with utterances, one should enclose the fire sternly.
Then one should give a fourfold oblation to Agni and the rest; then to the guardians of the quarters, with the sacred thread, an outer offering.

In the book of doctrine one should give the thread with measure. "Om Ham Bhuh svaha; Om Ham Bhuvah svaha; Om Ham Svah svaha; Om Ham Bhur Bhuvah Svah svaha" — having made the oblation with utterances, having given the four oblations,

Om Ham, to Agni, svaha; Om Ham, to Soma, svaha; Om Ham, to Agni-Soma, svaha; Om Ham, to Agni Svishtakrit, svaha. Having worshipped the teacher like Shiva with garments, ornaments and the like at length, his yearly ritual section and the rest is complete and fruitful.
Of whom the teacher is well pleased, so said the Supreme Lord. Thus having placed on the teacher the thread hanging on the heart,
having fed twice-born, one should devotedly give clothes and the rest: "By this gift, lord of gods, may Shiva be ever pleased with me."
Having devoutly done bathing and the rest in the morning, one should take away Shambhu's threads, worship him with eight flowers and dismiss him.
Having done the daily and occasional rites in detail as before, having placed the threads and bowed, one should worship Shiva in the fire.
Then one should offer the expiation with the missile-mantra and give the full oblation. The seeker of enjoyment should then offer the work to Shiva:
By your grace may this work not be a producer of fruit for me. The seeker of liberation: "May this work not bind me, lord."
Shiva in the fire one should unite with Shiva by the joining of channels. Having placed the mass of fire in the heart, one should dismiss the fire.
Having rinsed and entered within, the coverings along the pot, having united them with Shiva, one should dismiss with "Forgive."
Having dismissed the guardians of the world and the rest and taken the thread from Ishana, with Chandeshvara present, having done worship and given the thread,
one should offer him that remnant with the thread. Or one should worship Chanda on a platform as before by rule:
Whatever yearly work has been done by me, more or less, may it be complete for me at your command, lord Chanda.

Having thus informed the lord of the gods, having bowed and praised, one should dismiss him. Having left the remnant, pure, having bathed Shiva, one should worship; even standing five yojanas away, the thread in the presence of the teacher.
With the left head or with the stem; Dhatri in the north; the broken leaf in the south; in the east a flower for wearing;
fruit or root in a leaf-cup; then one should worship Shiva in the northeast. Having made the five limbs on the joined hands, having invited, one should place on the head:
You have been invited, lord of gods, by me in the morning, Lord; the gain of austerity is to be made; all is full at your command.
With the root-mantra, having covered the rest in the vessel, then the thread; in the morning, having bathed, one should worship the lord of the world with scent, flowers and the rest.
Having done the daily and occasional rite, one should then worship with damana; having taken the remaining handful, with the Self-knowledge Shivas,

with the root and the others up to Ishvara, then with the fourth handful: "Om Haum, to the lord of the sacrifice, fulfill the sacrifice; homage to the trident-bearer." Having worshipped Shiva and the fire and the teacher, one should inform:
Lord, whatever excess or deficiency was done by me, may all that be complete, and my damanaka. Having obtained the whole fruit arising from the month of Chaitra, one goes to heaven.
For enjoyment and liberation, first one should touch the Vardhani with the fist; one should offer the sword of knowledge to protect the pot's mouth.
One should place a hundred of the weapon and root-mantra in the pot; with a tenth of that, one should announce protection in the Vardhani:
As this sacrificial temple, O Lord, made with effort, is to be guarded by you, lord of the world, upholder of all sacrifices.
One should worship the Gana in Om, four-armed, in the northwest. Having worshipped Shiva on the platform, the man should go with arghya to the fire-pit.
Seated for the satisfaction of the mantras, having placed arghya, scent, ghee and the rest on the left, and fuel, darbha, sesame and the rest on the right,
having prepared the pit-fire, ladle, ghee and the rest as before and contemplated, one should worship Shiva in the heart-fire, chief, with face turned upward.
In one's own form, in Shiva's pot, on the platform, in the fire and the disciples, having placed by the placing of creation, having purified the path by rule,
having meditated on the pit's measure and the mouth, with heart-oblations as desired; the seed-syllables of the seven tongues of Agni are told for the oblation.
The last two syllables with the "Ra" and sixth vowel, joined with moon, bindu and crest — the tongue-seeds in order.
Hiranya, Vanaka, Rakta, Krishna, then Suprabha, Atirikta, Bahurupa — facing Rudra, Indra, Agni, and the other directions.
One should do the oblation with milk and sweets for pacification and prosperity; for malevolent rites with oil-cake, barley meal, husk and gruel,
with salts, mustard, buttermilk, pungent oil and thorns, with crooked fuel sticks, angry, one should worship with the Bhashya atom.
By oblation of kadamba buds a Yakshini is surely accomplished; bandhuka, kimshuka and the like one should offer for subjugation and attraction;
bilva for kingdom, for fortune patala and champaka; lotuses for universal sovereignty; foods for wealth;
durva for destroying disease, for subjugating all beings; priyangu and patali flowers, mango leaf: destroyer of fever;
Mrityunjaya conquers death; by sesame oblation there is growth; Rudra's peace is for all peace; now the topic is told.
With eight hundred oblations the root, and the limbs by a tenth part; one should satisfy with the root and give the full oblation as before.
Likewise for the entry of a disciple one should repeat a hundred for each disciple; for driving away bad omens and for making good omens
two hundred should be offered with the root-mantra as before. With the eight root-and-others weapon-mantras ending in svaha, one satisfaction at once;
with seeds enclosed by the crest, ending in Hrum phat, the kindling; and "Om Haum, to Shiva, svaha" and other mantras for satisfaction;
Om Hrum Hraum Hrim, to Shiva, Hrum phat and the like is the kindling. Then the pot washed with Shiva-water, covered with armor,
smeared with sandal and the rest, one should tie a bracelet on the neck. With armor- and missile-consecrated good darbha leaves for the success of the porridge,
when the seat is given with armor and the rest on a mandala made with half-moon, placed, in embodied form, one should worship Shiva with flowers of feeling;
or on a pot with mouth bound in cloth, with flowers from outside, on a hearth facing west, placed in human form,
with the ego-seed placed, purified by gazing and the rest, of the nature of dharma and adharma body, consecrated in human form,
